title: Taking the Bus: The Instrumental Suffix (-аар/-ээр/-оор/-өөр)
primaryPurpose: Introduce the instrumental case suffix to express vehicles, transport modes, and physical instruments of transit.
communicativeOutcome: Explain which mode of transport you use to commute across the city (e.g. 'Би автобусаар явна', 'Би машинаар ирлээ').
readingObjective: Read short commuters' forum sentences contrasting travel modes (bus vs walking vs car).
listeningObjective: Recognize the instrumental suffix when speakers state how they arrived at school or work.
writingObjective: Write 3 simple sentences declaring daily commute methods using instrumental case marking.
spokenProductionObjective: Answer prompts regarding how you travel to work or university using instrumental nouns.
pragmaticTarget: Stating transit choices plainly and neutrally without unnecessary hesitation.
reviewReason: Builds directly upon A1 public transit vocabulary by introducing the formal instrumental case.
audioPurpose: Model vowel harmony allomorphs of the instrumental case on stems ending in consonants and vowels.
successCriteria: Selects correct instrumental allomorph (-аар, -ээр, -оор, -өөр) based on root vowel harmony
Constructs well-formed SOV sentences specifying transit mode as instrumental adjunct
masteryEvidence: Produces 'Би өдөр бүр арван хоёр дугаар автобусаар явдаг' accurately matching vowel harmony.

title: Smart Card Tap & Bus Stops: U-Money in Practice
primaryPurpose: Introduce practical vocabulary for digital transit smart cards (U-Money), balance checks, and boarding etiquette.
communicativeOutcome: Purchase, tap, and reload a municipal bus card, and ask where to check card balance.
readingObjective: Read kiosk stickers instructing passengers where and how to reload U-Money cards.
listeningObjective: Understand convenience store cashier explaining minimum card reload amounts.
writingObjective: Note down card balance and bus line numbers in a pocket memo.
spokenProductionObjective: Ask a kiosk vendor to top up a transit card with a specified amount of tugriks.
pragmaticTarget: Handing over card and cash with respectful two-handed or right-hand elbow support gesture.
reviewReason: Connects money transactions from A1 canteen encounters to digital smart transit reloading.
audioPurpose: Demonstrate authentic fast speech customer requests at small street convenience kiosks.
successCriteria: Accurately names smart card components: цэнэглэх (top up), үлдэгдэл (balance), уншуулах (tap card)
Conducts a smooth kiosk transaction requesting a 5,000 or 10,000 MNT card recharge
masteryEvidence: Requests 'U-Money карт таван мянган төгрөгөөр цэнэглэж өгөөч' fluently at a sales counter.

title: Digital Transit Media: U-Money Smart Cards, Fares & Validation
primaryPurpose: Introduce vocabulary for electronic fare media, smart card readers, balance recharge points, and automated bus turnstiles.
communicativeOutcome: Purchase, reload, and tap a digital U-Money transit card when boarding municipal buses.
listeningObjective: Identify next stop name ('Дараагийн зогсоол...'), transfer alerts, and door closing warnings from onboard automated PA clips.
spokenProductionObjective: Confirm with fellow passenger if the bus stops at your target destination.
pragmaticTarget: Attuning ear to automated voice inflection and noisy bus engine acoustics.
reviewReason: Progresses from simple A1 stop name recognition to parsing compound automated PA sentences.
audioPurpose: Provide high-fidelity onboard recordings with authentic bus background ambient rumble and chime.
successCriteria: Identifies stop name following 'Дараагийн зогсоол' under simulated cabin engine noise
Extracts door safety warning 'Хаалга хаагдлаа, болгоомжтой байгаарай' without visual text
masteryEvidence: Correctly matches 4 recorded bus announcements to their corresponding route map stop sequences.

title: Deciphering Bus Shelter Route Diagrams & Operating Hours
primaryPurpose: Build reading skills for authentic municipal bus stop route placards, direction arrows, and first/last bus schedules.
communicativeOutcome: Read a bus shelter schedule to determine operating hours, route paths, and whether a bus runs on weekends.
readingObjective: Locate departure interval (зай/хүлээх хугацаа), terminal stop, and evening cutoff time on a bus route diagram.
writingObjective: Transcribe bus schedule operating window into a personal calendar entry.
spokenProductionObjective: Explain to a peer how often the bus runs and when the final bus departs.
pragmaticTarget: Extracting vital transit facts quickly from complex graphic layouts.
reviewReason: Integrates time/calendar terms from A1 with public transit schedule reading.
audioPurpose: Provide spoken pronunciation of route numbers and schedule captions.
successCriteria: Locates operating hours (e.g. 06:40 - 22:30) on a Cyrillic route graphic
Determines whether bus route runs straight along Peace Avenue or turns north towards Sansar
masteryEvidence: Identifies departure frequency and final evening run from an authentic Ulaanbaatar route diagram.

title: Which Bus Goes to the Central Post Office? Stop Inquiries
primaryPurpose: Develop interactive spoken ability to ask bystanders at a crowded stop which bus reaches a specific destination.
communicativeOutcome: Ask pedestrians for bus route advice, confirm if a bus goes through Sukhbaatar Square, and signal intent to alight.
listeningObjective: Follow a fellow passenger's spoken reply explaining which bus number to take and where to transfer.
spokenProductionObjective: Ask a fellow commuter: 'Уучлаарай, энэ автобус Төв шуудангаар дайрах уу?' and respond appropriately.
pragmaticTarget: Using polite attention getters ('Уучлаарай, танаас нэг зүйл асууж болох уу?') without being intrusive.
reviewReason: Spirals polar question syntax (уу/үү) into real-time transit route inquiries.
audioPurpose: Simulate natural conversational pace between two commuters at an outdoor winter bus stop.
successCriteria: Asks whether a specific bus line passes a landmark using polite particle and instrumental case
Understands bystander's recommendation to wait for another line or transfer at the next stop
masteryEvidence: Participates in an unscripted roleplay asking how to reach the Central Post Office from 120 Myangat.

title: Transit SMS: Coordinating Bus Commute Times with a Friend
primaryPurpose: Synthesize instrumental case, bus route numbers, and arrival predictions in short personal messaging.
communicativeOutcome: Compose a brief message informing a friend which bus you boarded and at which stop to meet.
readingObjective: Read a friend's incoming SMS inquiring about your current bus stop location.
writingObjective: Write a 3-sentence SMS stating which bus you are on, your current stop, and estimated arrival.
pragmaticTarget: Using concise digital text conventions while maintaining accurate grammatical case endings.
reviewReason: Combines ongoing progressive aspect (-ж байна) with instrumental transit markings.
audioPurpose: Read back written messages for ear training.
successCriteria: Drafts a coherent text message indicating bus number in instrumental case
Coordinates arrival time with meeting place using locative case correctly
masteryEvidence: Writes 'Би 2-р автобусаар явж байна. Их дэлгүүрийн зогсоол дээр 10 минутын дараа уулзъя' without grammatical error.

title: Directing the Driver: The Directional Suffix (-руу/-рүү)
primaryPurpose: Introduce the directional case suffix (-руу/-рүү) after consonants and vowels to indicate orientation and movement towards landmarks.
communicativeOutcome: Instruct a taxi driver to turn or head towards specific landmarks (e.g. 'Баруун гар тийшээ, их дэлгүүр лүү эргээрэй').
readingObjective: Read navigation app prompts specifying turns toward key monuments and thoroughfares.
listeningObjective: Distinguish between directional (-руу) and locative (-д) markers in taxi dispatch instructions.
writingObjective: Write 3 directional commands directing a driver toward a specific street or landmark.
spokenProductionObjective: Direct a driver in real time: 'Гэрлэн дохиогоор зүүн тийш, эмнэлэг рүү эргээрэй'.
registerTarget: Everyday spoken directive register with polite imperatives
pragmaticTarget: Giving clear, calm spatial instructions to drivers without abrupt hesitation.
reviewReason: Builds on spatial postpositions by introducing synthetic directional case morphology.
audioPurpose: Model vowel harmony choices (-руу vs -рүү) after various noun codas.
successCriteria: Correctly selects -руу or -рүү depending on back/front vocalic harmony of noun root
Accurately guides vehicle movement toward landmarks using directional case
masteryEvidence: Produces 'Төв талбай руу чигээрээ яваад, баруун тийшээ эргээрэй' with flawless case marking.

title: Hailing Street Cabs: Raising Hands & Landmark Waypoints
primaryPurpose: Introduce essential colloquial vocabulary for hailing informal street cabs, negotiating drop-off points, and using landmarks.
communicativeOutcome: Hail an informal street taxi, state destination by prominent landmark, and negotiate a per-kilometer fare.
readingObjective: Read taxi app rate cards detailing base fare and nighttime surcharges.
listeningObjective: Comprehend taxi driver asking 'Хаашаа явах вэ? Хэдэн төгрөгөөр явах юм?' through car window.
writingObjective: Note down street intersections and agreed taxi fares.
spokenProductionObjective: Hail a car and state: 'Багшийн дээд орно, хоёр мянгаар явах уу?' clearly.
pragmaticTarget: Quick roadside verbal negotiation with driver with window rolled down.
reviewReason: Applies transactional negotiation techniques to urban transport services.
audioPurpose: Simulate authentic street side roadside noise and driver banter.
successCriteria: Correctly names common urban waypoints: уулзвар (intersection), гүүр (bridge), гэрлэн дохио (traffic light)
Negotiates ride terms within 10 seconds of car stopping
masteryEvidence: Successfully negotiates destination and fare with simulated street cab driver.

title: Acoustic Lab: Street Hailing Ambient Shouts & Approaching Cabs
primaryPurpose: Develop acoustic discrimination for short shouted landmark names and cab honks in dense street traffic.
communicativeOutcome: Guide driver through side streets, ask to pull over right after an intersection, and request change.
listeningObjective: Identify passenger destination cries ('Урагшаа!', 'Төв талбай!') over engine noise.
spokenProductionObjective: Instruct driver: 'Энэ булангаар баруун тийшээ эргээд, эмийн сангийн хажууд буулгачих'.
pragmaticTarget: Using softening converbs (-чих) and polite imperatives (-аарай) to ensure pleasant cooperation.
reviewReason: Combines polite imperative suffixation (-аарай) with rapid navigational directives.
audioPurpose: Deliver realistic passenger-driver dialogue with typical turns of speech and hesitation.
successCriteria: Directs driver through 2 consecutive turns without pauses causing missed turns
Politely asks driver to stop near a specific building entrance
masteryEvidence: Guides cab to drop-off point and completes payment exchange without English intervention.

title: Acoustic Lab: Radio Dispatch Audio & Fare Calculations
primaryPurpose: Sharpen listening comprehension of authentic taxi radio chatter, automated dispatch updates, and fare calculation disputes.
communicativeOutcome: Extract pickup address, destination landmark, and calculated fare from authentic taxi dispatch communications.
listeningObjective: Extract pickup address, kilometer meter reading, and total fare from taxi dispatch radio audio.
spokenProductionObjective: Summarize the overheard taxi dispute to a partner in 2 Mongolian sentences.
pragmaticTarget: Extracting key spatial and numeric information despite low-bandwidth audio distortion.
reviewReason: Reinforces rapid mental decoding of multi-digit currency numbers from A1.
audioPurpose: Acoustic dispatch audio with radio squelch, background traffic horns, and rapid Mongolian numbers.
successCriteria: Accurately extracts building number, street landmark, and price from dispatch audio clips
Determines whether driver accepts or rejects passenger pickup request
masteryEvidence: Logs 3 distinct radio dispatch tasks with 100% correct landmark and fare transcription.

title: Written Micro-Directions: Dropping a Text Pin for Ride Pickup
primaryPurpose: Synthesize directional case (-руу/-рүү), spatial adverbs, and landmark descriptions in written ride-hailing notes.
communicativeOutcome: Write clear pickup instructions in a ride app chat explaining exactly where you are waiting.
readingObjective: Read driver's written text query: 'Та байрны аль талд нь зогсож байна вэ?'.
writingObjective: Compose concise written instructions detailing your precise curb location, clothing, and surrounding signs.
registerTarget: Direct and polite digital written chat
pragmaticTarget: Providing unambiguous location cues in minimum words to prevent driver circling.
reviewReason: Applies postpositional spatial phrases (өмнө, хажууд, хойно) to real-time written driver communication.
audioPurpose: Audio playback of user drafted pickup messages.
successCriteria: Writes a 2-3 sentence location note containing directional suffix and spatial postposition
Accurately guides vehicle toward building entrance without ambiguity
masteryEvidence: Drafts 'Би төв хаалганы баруун талд, кофе шопын үүдэнд хар куртиктэй зогсож байна' correctly.

title: By Train, By Bus, By Card: Instrumental Case of Means (-аар4)
primaryPurpose: Introduce the instrumental case suffix (-аар / -ээр / -оор / -өөр) for expressing means of transit, tools, and methods of payment in intercity travel.
communicativeOutcome: Specify transit vehicles and transaction methods across provinces (e.g. 'Бид Дархан руу хурдан галт тэргээр явна', 'Би тасалбарын үнийг картаар төлнө').
readingObjective: Read passenger statement bubbles explaining reasons and transit methods for boarding intercity transport.
listeningObjective: Identify vehicle noun and instrumental suffix in passengers' recorded travel methods.
writingObjective: Formulate 3 sentences combining destination in directional case and transit vehicle in instrumental case.
spokenProductionObjective: Explain to a ticket agent how and by what vehicle you wish to travel to Darkhan or Erdenet.
pragmaticTarget: Specifying transit modes and payment methods concisely during ticket purchasing.
reviewReason: Expands instrumental case from basic transport nouns to broader means, methods, and transaction modes.
audioPurpose: Model quadruple vowel harmony of the instrumental suffix (-аар, -ээр, -оор, -өөр).
successCriteria: Applies correct allomorph of -аар4 according to root stem harmony
Expresses valid instrument or transit means modifying movement verb
masteryEvidence: Produces 'Бид Дархан руу хурдан галт тэргээр явахаар шийдсэн' accurately.

title: Dragon Terminal & Railway Station: Intercity Travel Hubs
primaryPurpose: Introduce core vocabulary for regional transport hubs, rail berths, sleeper compartments, and long-distance buses.
communicativeOutcome: Distinguish between train carriage types, understand baggage weight allowances, and navigate bus platforms.
readingObjective: Read terminal floor directories locating ticket windows, waiting halls, and luggage storage.
listeningObjective: Understand baggage clerk stating overweight luggage fees per kilogram.
writingObjective: List essential long-distance travel items and luggage labels in Cyrillic.
spokenProductionObjective: Inquire about sleeper berth options (купе vs плацкарт) at the station inquiry window.
pragmaticTarget: Clear articulation in noisy transport terminal halls.
reviewReason: Expands city transit vocabulary to provincial long-distance transit.
audioPurpose: Acoustic modeling of terminal announcements and ticketing clerk voice.
successCriteria: Identifies key carriage categories: купе (soft sleeper), плацкарт (hard sleeper), нийтийн (general)
Distinguishes Dragon terminal intercity coach gates from railway platforms
masteryEvidence: Correctly names and classifies 8 intercity travel items and locations.

title: Platform Audio Lab: Departure Calls & Track Announcements
primaryPurpose: Develop acoustic comprehension of reverberant public railway station and long-distance bus terminal announcements.
communicativeOutcome: Extract train/bus route numbers, track numbers, departure delays, and boarding calls from live public address audio.
listeningObjective: Extract train number, track/platform number, departure time, and delay duration from platform PA recordings.
spokenProductionObjective: Inform traveling companion of platform assignment and departure time change.
pragmaticTarget: Parsing high-reverberation station audio with echo and acoustic distortion.
reviewReason: Applies clock time listening comprehension to high-stakes transit schedule announcements.
audioPurpose: Provide reverberant station audio with realistic echo, platform bells, and diesel train engine sounds.
successCriteria: Identifies train number and departure track from simulated station broadcast
Catches 15-minute delay notice without repeating the audio clip more than twice
masteryEvidence: Fills in complete boarding table (train #, track, departure, destination) from 3 audio clips.

title: Deciphering Mongolian Railway Tickets & Departure Boards
primaryPurpose: Develop targeted reading skills for official Mongolian railway e-tickets, carriage numbers, berth codes, and baggage vouchers.
communicativeOutcome: Inspect a printed railway ticket or digital PDF voucher to find carriage number, berth, passenger name, and departure date.
readingObjective: Locate departure date, train number, carriage (вагон), upper/lower berth (дээд/доод ор), and passport details on ticket PDF.
writingObjective: Transcribe critical ticket numbers into personal travel log.
spokenProductionObjective: Explain ticket seat allocation to a fellow traveler in Mongolian.
pragmaticTarget: Verifying ticket authenticity and ensuring passport name matches ticket Cyrillic spelling.
reviewReason: Recycles date and month reading skills on authentic government ticket vouchers.
audioPurpose: Pronounce formal administrative ticket labels.
successCriteria: Locates carriage and seat number on an authentic Mongolian Railway (УБТЗ) ticket
Distinguishes upper berth (дээд ор) from lower berth (доод ор)
masteryEvidence: Answers 5 comprehension questions based on a sample Ulaanbaatar-Sainshand e-ticket.

title: At the Ticket Window: Booking Sleeper Berths & Round-Trips
primaryPurpose: Simulate spoken interaction at an intercity bus or train ticket window, negotiating departure times and berth positions.
communicativeOutcome: Purchase round-trip tickets to an aimag center, specify lower berth preference, and ask about cancellation policies.
listeningObjective: Understand ticketing agent presenting remaining seat choices and departure times.
spokenProductionObjective: Request round-trip tickets: 'Эрдэнэт рүү хоёр талын купе тасалбар хоёрыг авъя. Доод ор байна уу?'.
pragmaticTarget: Checking ticket details before stepping away from the glass partition counter.
reviewReason: Uses volitional verb forms (-я/-е) for transactional requests at ticket counters.
audioPurpose: Model fast, professional cashier responses through ticket glass microphone.
successCriteria: Negotiates ticket purchase including date, destination, class, and seat position
Confirms return travel date using calendar vocabulary and volitional forms
masteryEvidence: Completes full simulated ticket booking dialogue including ID check and payment.

title: Intercity Travel Plan: Writing Itinerary & Packing Essentials
primaryPurpose: Consolidate purposive converb, transportation nouns, and schedule timings in a comprehensive written travel plan.
communicativeOutcome: Write a 5-6 sentence travel itinerary detailing departure station, transit purpose, stops, and arrival checklist.
readingObjective: Read a sample rural expedition schedule to emulate chronological layout.
writingObjective: Draft a complete personal itinerary using purposive converbs (-хаар) and sequential converbs (-аад).
pragmaticTarget: Clear chronological structuring of travel events and packing requirements.
reviewReason: Links sequential converb (-аад) from A1 with A2 purposive converb (-хаар) in written prose.
audioPurpose: Read back generated travel plan for self-correction.
successCriteria: Produces written itinerary with correct time stamps, departure locations, and purposive verbs
Integrates at least one sequential converb and one purposive converb
masteryEvidence: Writes: 'Бид маргааш өглөө 8 цагт галт тэргээр Дархан руу найзтайгаа уулзахаар явна' and subsequent steps correctly.

title: Like and Similar To: Comparative Adverbials (Шиг, Адил, Мэт)
primaryPurpose: Introduce comparative adverbials and postpositions (шиг, адил, мэт) to describe landmarks, visual likeness, and relative scale.
communicativeOutcome: Describe building landmarks by analogy (e.g. 'Тэр барилга цамхаг шиг харагдана', 'Номын сангийн адил том байшин').
readingObjective: Read tourist blurbs describing Ulaanbaatar architecture using visual analogies (Blue Sky Tower like a sail).
listeningObjective: Recognize comparative particles (шиг/адил) when pedestrians describe building facades.
writingObjective: Write 3 comparative sentences identifying buildings by resemblance.
spokenProductionObjective: Explain to a visitor: 'Тэр хөх шилтэй байшин Blue Sky шиг харагдаж байна'.
pragmaticTarget: Using vivid visual metaphors to make wayfinding cues memorable.
reviewReason: Complements the ablative of comparison from A1 with postpositional comparative constructions.
audioPurpose: Model clitic-like prosodic integration of 'шиг' after nominal phrases.
successCriteria: Distinguishes syntactic use of 'шиг' (postpositional) vs 'адил' (independent adverbial)
Forms well-formed comparative descriptive phrases identifying visual landmarks
masteryEvidence: Produces 'Энэ өндөр барилга нь цирк шиг дугуй оройтой' correctly.

title: Alleyways, Squares & Underpasses: Urban Topography
primaryPurpose: Introduce spatial vocabulary for navigating pedestrian zones, subterranean underpasses (нүхэн гарц), alleys, and monumental statues.
communicativeOutcome: Name and recognize complex pedestrian infrastructure, crosswalks, traffic circles, and public statues.
readingObjective: Read pedestrian directional signs on Peace Avenue directing foot traffic to underpasses.
listeningObjective: Understand street crossing safety announcements at pedestrian crossings.
writingObjective: List 6 pedestrian landmarks encountered on a daily walking route.
spokenProductionObjective: Describe a walking shortcut using alleyways and underground passageways.
pragmaticTarget: Accurate spatial precision in dense urban neighborhoods.
reviewReason: Expands A1 spatial relational nouns to modern built environment vocabulary.
audioPurpose: Pronounce compound spatial terms with stress on initial syllable.
successCriteria: Accurately defines нүхэн гарц (underpass), явган хүний зам (sidewalk), уулзвар (crossroad)
Uses newly introduced landmarks in locative sentences
masteryEvidence: Identifies and explains 5 pedestrian map symbols correctly in Mongolian.

title: Turn Past the Statues: Interactive Multi-Step Directions
primaryPurpose: Master asking for and executing multi-step pedestrian directions involving at least three spatial transitions.

pragmaticTarget: Using active backchanneling ('Тэгээд цаашаа юу?', 'Аан, ойлголоо') to confirm direction comprehension.
reviewReason: Links sequential motion verbs using coordinating converbs (-ж/-ч).
audioPurpose: Deliver authentic multi-speaker dialogue recorded outdoors on a windy city street.
successCriteria: Produces a coherent 3-clause instruction connecting sequential turns and landmarks
Repeats back directions to confirm comprehension before departing
masteryEvidence: Guides interlocutor accurately from Sukhbaatar statue to the National Museum of Mongolia.

title: Deciphering City Center Walking Maps & Heritage Trails
primaryPurpose: Develop reading skills for municipal walking tour brochures, monument plaques, and walking route legends.
communicativeOutcome: Read a historical downtown walking circuit map, identifying key architectural highlights and distance markers.
readingObjective: Read a 100-word historical walking trail brochure detailing distances, notable facades, and rest areas.
writingObjective: Annotate map landmarks with brief Cyrillic descriptive notes.
spokenProductionObjective: Explain to a companion which historical building is next on the walking trail.

audioPurpose: Narrate text excerpts from historical walking trail guide.
successCriteria: Answers 4 detailed questions about walking distances and historical highlights from brochure
Traces the walking path accurately based on textual instructions
masteryEvidence: Matches 5 historical descriptions to their corresponding map pins on an Ulaanbaatar city center map.

title: Acoustic Wayfinding Lab: Parsing Directions in City Noise
primaryPurpose: Develop focused acoustic decoding of rapid spoken directions against realistic ambient background noise of horns, wind, and footsteps.

spokenProductionObjective: Verify directions with interlocutor: 'Таны хэлснээр бол, гэрлэн дохиогоор зүүн эргэх үү?'.

reviewReason: Tests locative discrimination under adverse acoustic conditions.
audioPurpose: Realistic audio captured on Peace Avenue with traffic hum, footsteps, and wind noise.
successCriteria: Identifies correct sequence of turns (left, straight, right) from 4 audio clips
Extracts approximate walking distance (зуун метр, хоёр зуун метр) without text
masteryEvidence: Accurately maps out pedestrian route from audio recording without errors.

title: Wayfinding Portfolio: Drafting Written Walking Directions
primaryPurpose: Synthesize comparative particles, directional suffixes, spatial postpositions, and landmarks into a written guide for foreign guests.

successCriteria: Writes a coherent sequential guide detailing at least 3 distinct turns and landmarks
Correctly incorporates at least one comparative particle and one directional suffix
masteryEvidence: Produces complete written guide: 'Буудлаас гараад зүүн тийш алхаарай. Цамхаг шиг өндөр барилга өнгөрөөд...' flawlessly.

title: Immediate Incidents: The Witnessed Recent Past (-лаа/-лээ/-лоо/-лөө)
primaryPurpose: Introduce the witnessed recent past tense suffix (-лаа4) to report immediate events, sudden delays, and newly observed breakdowns.

successCriteria: Selects correct vowel harmony allomorph (-лаа, -лээ, -лоо, -лөө) based on verbal root
Contrasts immediate witnessed past (-лаа) with resultative past (-сан)

title: Deciphering Road Condition Bulletins, Traffic Radio Alerts & Detours

Uses newly introduced delay nouns in complete sentences
masteryEvidence: Accurately categorizes 6 transit disruption scenarios into mechanical vs infrastructure causes.

title: Acoustic Lab: Radio Traffic Bulletins & Rush-Hour Updates
primaryPurpose: Develop acoustic listening comprehension of authentic Ulaanbaatar radio traffic broadcasts (FM 106.3 / Авто радио).
